minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved drainage and Hemlock Drive, a dock, Table Rock trailhead parking and 213 Electric Ave, and sought peer review for 221 Electric Ave.
minutes.summary: The commission held hearings on five projects. It approved the 32 Hemlock Drive pipe replacement, a negative determination for a 76 Laurel Lane dock, the Table Rock trailhead parking area, and the 213 Electric Ave notice of intent. It voted to require third-party peer review of Riverfront status and wetland flags at 221 Electric Ave and continued that hearing to April 2nd. Members also discussed using peer review more often, an April 30th training time, and Earth Day plans.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to require third-party peer review, at the applicant's cost, of Riverfront status and wetland flags at 221 Electric Ave.
The 221 Electric Ave hearing was continued to April 2nd.
The commission approved notices of intent for the 32 Hemlock Drive drainage pipe replacement, the Table Rock trailhead parking area, and 213 Electric Ave.
The commission issued a negative determination for a dock at 76 Laurel Lane, using the already-disturbed area as the access route.
Members discussed using third-party peer review more often, including a standing bid for an on-call engineer, and aimed for a 5 PM start to an April 30th training.

why_it_matters: Peer review is paid for by the applicant under the bylaw, so more frequent use shifts review costs from the town to project applicants and could lengthen timelines for projects near wetlands.
The Table Rock trailhead parking area is on conservation land that a member noted was bought with taxpayer money and only partly funded by a grant, so residents have a stake in how it is developed.
watch_next: April 2nd: the continued hearing on 221 Electric Ave, after the peer review request for quotes, and the continued hearing on 390 Howard Street.
April 30th: commission training, with a 5 PM start to be confirmed with absent members.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the outcome of all six motions and on the main attendees, but the official minutes record the votes tersely and several of our details do not appear in them. The most important difference is the 221 Electric Ave peer review motion: ours says it covers Riverfront applicability and flags 102 through 104 at the applicant's cost, while the official text says only "peer review and replacement of flags 104-104".
